01 / THE QUESTION

What needed to work?

A manipulated video can look plausible frame by frame. Video-level classification needs a consistent preprocessing and aggregation path.

An OpenCV preprocessing pipeline and MobileNetV2 transfer-learning workflow for authentic-versus-manipulated video classification.

03 / THE ENGINEERING

The decision behind it.

Sample eight frames, use a detected face when available, resize to 128 × 128, then aggregate the three largest frame scores.

  1. 01Input video
  2. 02OpenCV frame extraction
  3. 03MobileNetV2 classifier
  4. 04Video-level prediction
  • Used MobileNetV2 transfer learning for authentic-versus-manipulated video classification.
  • Built an OpenCV preprocessing pipeline to extract video frames and prepare TensorFlow inputs.
  • Combined frame-level predictions into video-level authenticity predictions.
PythonTensorFlowMobileNetV2OpenCVNumPy

04 / THE EVIDENCE

What the work demonstrates.

The preview executes the repository’s top-three aggregation rule. Its scores are examples; model weights and a measured accuracy are not supplied.

The repository contains training and prediction scripts. The cinematic walkthrough executes the same top-three aggregation rule on clearly labeled example scores.

BOUNDARY OF THE EVIDENCE

The trained model weights are absent from the public repository. This portfolio does not claim live deepfake inference or a measured accuracy.
